summary.abstract_hr: Na susretu molitvene zajednice Nanovo rođeni Goran Ćurković iznosi svoje životno svjedočanstvo, koje dijeli na život bez Boga i život s Bogom. Opisuje djetinjstvo u Splitu u obitelji bez vjere, obiteljske tragedije, pokušaj samoubojstva u 13. godini nakon kojeg mu je metak ostao u glavi, ovisnost o drogi i alkoholu, zatvor, psihijatriju te devet godina života na ulici. Prekretnica dolazi nakon molitve Zdravomarije i susreta sa ženom koja ga šalje u Međugorje, gdje ulazi u zajednicu Cenacolo, miri se s ocem, zapošljava se uz pomoć fratara i upoznaje svoju buduću suprugu Katarinu. Danas je ikonograf, otac petero djece i svakodnevno svjedoči hodočasnicima, a posebno mu je drago svjedočiti u zatvorima i na psihijatriji.
key_points: Goran je odrastao u katoličkoj obitelji bez molitve i odlaska u crkvu, a obitelj su pogodile tragedije: sestra je poginula pavši s petog kata, brat je ostao gluhonijem, a majka je pala u depresiju i alkoholizam te umrla kad je Goranu bilo 13 godina.

Na prvu godišnjicu majčine smrti pucao je sebi u glavu; metak mu je ostao u glavi, a nakon toga je počeo s tabletama, marihuanom i heroinom, krao je, bio u zatvoru i na psihijatriji, ranio oca nožem i devet godina živio na ulici.

Nakon noći u kojoj je shvatio da je sam kriv za svoj život i počeo moliti Zdravomariju, žena Dijana pronašla ga je u parku, sredila mu dokumente i poslala ga u Međugorje, gdje je odmah primljen u zajednicu.

U zajednici ga je promijenio primjer momaka koji su umjesto njega radili u kamenolomu, a nakon molitve i noćnog klečanja u kapeli otac ga je neočekivano posjetio te su se pomirili; otac mu je rekao da se za njega obitelj već godinama moli.

Nakon četiri godine zajednice uz pomoć fra Slavka Barbarića dobio je posao čišćenja zahoda u Međugorju, gdje je upoznao Katarinu, Čehinju koja se molila za poziv u redovništvo; vjenčali su se 3. lipnja 2000. u crkvi sv. Jakova u Međugorju i imaju petero djece.
Kaže da od dolaska u Međugorje nije imao epileptičnih napada, da nikad nije imao napast vratiti se drogi, a maćeha je devet godina svaki mjesec plaćala misu za njegovo obraćenje.
Danas je ikonograf i svakodnevno drži po tri do četiri svjedočanstva; zajedno sa suprugom uputio je više od 60 mladih u zajednicu, a najdraže mu je svjedočiti u zatvorima i na psihijatriji.

key_points_en: Goran grew up in a Catholic family without prayer and going to church, and the family was struck by tragedies: his sister died falling from the fifth floor, his brother was left deaf-mute, and his mother fell into depression and alcoholism and died when Goran was 13 years old.

On the first anniversary of his mother's death he shot himself in the head; the bullet remained in his head, and after that he started with pills, marijuana, and heroin, he stole, was in prison and in psychiatry, wounded his father with a knife, and lived on the street for nine years.

After a night in which he realized that he himself was to blame for his life and began to pray the Hail Mary, a woman named Dijana found him in a park, arranged his documents, and sent him to Međugorje, where he was immediately received into the community.

In the community, he was changed by the example of guys who worked in the quarry instead of him, and after prayer and nighttime kneeling in the chapel his father unexpectedly visited him and they reconciled; his father told him that the family had already been praying for him for years.

After four years in the community, with the help of fra Slavko Barbarić he got a job cleaning toilets in Međugorje, where he met Katarina, a Czech woman who was praying for a religious vocation; they were married on June 3, 2000, in the Church of St. James in Međugorje and have five children.

He says that since arriving in Međugorje he has had no epileptic seizures, that he has never had the temptation to return to drugs, and for nine years his stepmother paid for a Mass each month for his conversion.

Today he is an iconographer and gives three to four testimonies daily; together with his wife, he has directed more than 60 young people into the community, and he loves most to testify in prisons and in psychiatry.

summary.abstract_en: At a meeting of the Nanovo rođeni prayer community, Goran Ćurković shares his life testimony, which he divides into a life without God and a life with God. He describes his childhood in Split in a family without faith, family tragedies, a suicide attempt at age 13 after which a bullet remained in his head, addiction to drugs and alcohol, prison, psychiatry, and nine years of living on the street. The turning point comes after praying the Hail Mary and an encounter with a woman who sends him to Međugorje, where he enters the Cenacolo community, reconciles with his father, gets a job with the help of the friars, and meets his future wife Katarina. Today he is an iconographer, father of five children, and daily testifies to pilgrims, and he is especially glad to testify in prisons and in psychiatry.
